subject: MAP: benchmarking deliverables & packaging for pilot close
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: benchmarking deliverables & packaging for pilot close

Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Per our MAP (mutual action plan) milestone toward the pilot commitment, here’s the proposed benchmarking plan and the packaging we’ll deliver for your review:

Objectives
- Validate latency (p95), throughput, and time-to-first-token (TTFT) for the 3 workload classes you shared (docs-indexing, search-retrieval, interactive chat).
- Confirm concurrency envelope and degradation profile at target QPS.
- Produce executive-friendly artifacts you can share with procurement/IT.

Benchmark plan (high level)
- Scenarios: 3 workload profiles using your sample prompts (we’ll reuse the prompt sets from the evaluation plan you provided).
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, TTFT, tokens-per-second, max sustainable throughput (rps), error rate, and cost-per-1k-tokens estimate.
- Concurrency sweep: single-connection to 128 concurrent connections (stepwise: 1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128).
- Environment: dedicated dev pool in us-west-2, Redwood Dedicated with pinned model v1.2-quantized.
- Acceptance targets (MAP-aligned): p95 < 120ms for short-chat; TTFT < 40ms; sustained throughput >= 800 rps for retrieval workload at 64 concurrency.

Deliverables (packaging)
- Slide deck: one executive summary + 3 appendix slides with raw plots.
- CSV exports: raw per-request CSV, aggregated summary CSV, and per-scenario concurrency CSV.
- Dashboard link: Grafana panel with time-series for latency and request rate.
- Exec one-pager: single-page summary for procurement.

Timeline (MAP dates)
- 2026-05-26: begin runs (smoke tests + baseline).
- 2026-05-28: full sweep and export.
- 2026-05-30: package deliverables (slides, CSVs, dashboard snapshot) + sync.
- 2026-06-02: pilot kickoff / DocuSign signature target.

Action items for this thread
- Sarah: confirm the sample prompt set + whether we should include an additional long-context scenario.
- Tom: please share any additional SLO thresholds beyond the acceptance targets above.
- Laura / Vivek: will own execution and packaging (ETA 5/30).

I’ll attach the initial skeleton slide deck and a blank CSV template to this thread tomorrow.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: benchmarking deliverables & packaging for pilot close

Ben —

Thanks, that plan looks good and maps to our procurement asks. Quick clarifications:

- For TTFT: are you measuring from request accept to first token, or from TCP connect? We care about end-user perceived latency (so request accept -> first token is fine).
- Concurrency sweep: confirm you’ll run with realistic client arrival patterns (poisson-ish) rather than perfectly steady threads — that will matter for our internal load tests.
- Please include the aggregated CSV with both raw per-request rows and per-minute rollups so our perf team can re-check.

We confirm the prompt sets attached to the eval plan — no long-context scenario required for the pilot (we can add later).

If you can get the deliverables packaged and the slide deck to us by 5/30 we can present to procurement on 6/1.

Sarah Jenkins
VP of Product | Acme Health
sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: benchmarking deliverables & packaging for pilot close (internal)

Ben / Vivek —

We completed the full sweep this morning. Attached are the draft artifacts:
- acme_benchmark_results_20260530.csv (raw per-request + per-minute aggregated sheets) [attachment stub: 2.1MB CSV]
- acme_map_slide_deck_v1.pptx [attachment stub: 3.8MB PPTX]
- exec one-pager: acme_exec_onepager.pdf [attachment stub: 220KB PDF]

Quick highlights from the runs (summary, keep for the deck):
- Retrieval workload (scenario B): sustained 820 rps at 64 concurrency, error rate 0.4%, p95 = 118ms, p50 = 42ms.
- Interactive chat (scenario A): TTFT measured as request-accept->first-token = median 28ms, p95 = 36ms.
- Long-tail concurrency: at 128 concurrent connections we saw tail latency jump (p95 ~ 410ms) but throughput plateaued; recommend we show both recommended and stressed profiles in the appendix.

Notes on CSVs: per-request rows include timestamp, scenario, concurrency, latency_ms, ttft_ms, tokens_out, error_flag, cost_est_usd. Aggregates have per-minute medians and p95s.

Dashboard: created a read-only Grafana snapshot and added it to the MAP artifacts folder. Link below.

I’ll push the slide deck with one-slide exec summary at the top plus three appendix slides showing concurrency sweep plots. Let me know if procurement wants different charting styles.

Laura Bennett
